action: Visualize the anatomical orientation of the kidney relative to the body.
interpretation: Recall that the upper pole of the kidney is slightly more posterior, while the lower pole is more anterior.

action: Adjust the transducer to an oblique position.
interpretation: Match the probe axis to the oblique lie of the kidney (posterior upper pole, anterior lower pole).

action: Obtain the standard view of the kidney.
interpretation: Identify the kidney and visualize the spleen within this window.

action: Sweep through the kidney in its entirety from lateral to medial.
interpretation: Ensure complete coverage of the renal parenchyma during the sagittal/oblique sweep.

action: Look at the probe and rotate 90 degrees from the sagittal image to obtain a transverse view.
interpretation: Transition from the longitudinal axis to the transverse axis of the left kidney.

action: Sweep the probe all the way up to the top (superior) and down to the lower pole (inferior) of the left kidney.
interpretation: Visualize the full transverse extent of the kidney from the top to the bottom.

action: Assess the image for acoustic shadowing or obstruction.
interpretation: Note that you may encounter rib artifacts obscuring the transverse picture.

action: If the image is obscured, utilize the intercostal space and sweep through it.
interpretation: Improve visualization of the upper or lower pole by avoiding rib shadows.

action: Continue scanning in the transverse window.
interpretation: Identify the spleen again within this transverse view.
